name: Shortest Walk to the Packing Desk
description:
A picker robot stands on the floor of an Amazon fulfilment centre. The floor is a grid of r rows and c columns. Each cell is one of:
'.' an open floor cell
'#' a storage rack (the robot cannot enter it)
'S' the robot's start cell (exactly one)
'D' the packing desk (exactly one)

In one step the robot moves to the cell directly up, down, left or right, if that cell is inside the grid and is not a rack. Print the minimum number of steps the robot needs to reach the packing desk. If the desk cannot be reached, print -1.

Input: The first line has two integers r and c. Each of the next r lines is a string of c characters from '.', '#', 'S', 'D'.
Output: A single integer, the minimum number of steps, or -1.

Constraints:
- 1 <= r, c <= 200
- The grid has exactly one 'S' and exactly one 'D'

Amazon OA pattern: shortest path on a grid with BFS (grid BFS is among the most reported Amazon OA topics, Aug-Nov 2026).

test_cases.description: Path S(0,0) → (1,0) → (1,1) → (2,1) → (2,2) → (2,3) → (1,3)=D takes 6 steps; the rack column blocks any shorter way.
The rack column '#' cuts S off from D completely, so the answer is -1.

name: Wi-Fi Rollout Across the Office
description:
Amazon's new Hyderabad office is laid out as a grid of r rows and c columns. Each cell is:
'.' a desk
'#' a concrete wall
'R' a Wi-Fi router (there can be zero, one or many)

At minute 0 every router cell has signal. Every minute, signal spreads from each cell that has it to the cells directly up, down, left and right of it, but never into or through a wall. Routers also pass signal on, just like desks.

The IT team wants two numbers:
1. The number of minutes after which every desk that will ever get signal has it (print 0 if no desk ever gets signal).
2. The number of desks that never get signal.

Input: The first line has two integers r and c. Each of the next r lines is a string of c characters from '.', '#', 'R'.
Output: Two integers separated by a space: the minutes, then the number of desks without signal.

Constraints:
- 1 <= r, c <= 200
- The number of routers can be 0 or as large as the grid

Amazon OA pattern: multi-source BFS (spread from many starting cells at once).

test_cases.description: The desk in row 1, column 3 is 4 moves from either router because walls block the short way, so full coverage takes 4 minutes. Every desk gets signal, so the answer is 4 0.
The 3 desks next to the router get signal within 2 minutes; the 7 desks on the right are walled off and never get signal, so the answer is 2 7.

name: Unserved Pockets After the Drone Launch
description:
Amazon is launching drone delivery over a town drawn as a grid of r rows and c columns. Each cell is:
'.' a house
'#' a no-fly tower (drones can never enter it)
'H' a drone hub (zero or more)

A drone starts at any hub and in one move can fly to any of the 8 neighbouring cells (up, down, left, right and the 4 diagonals), as long as that cell is inside the grid and is not a tower. A house is served if some hub can reach it in at most K moves. Every other house (too far, or impossible to reach) is unserved.

The planning team groups unserved houses into pockets: two unserved houses are in the same pocket if you can walk from one to the other moving only up, down, left or right through unserved houses. Print the number of pockets and the number of houses in the largest pocket (print 0 0 if every house is served).

Input: The first line has three integers r, c and K. Each of the next r lines is a string of c characters from '.', '#', 'H'.
Output: Two integers separated by a space: the number of pockets, then the size of the largest pocket.

Constraints:
- 1 <= r, c <= 200
- 0 <= K <= 40000
- Drones fly in 8 directions, but pockets are grouped in 4 directions

Amazon OA pattern: multi-source BFS combined with counting connected groups (as in Minimum Grid Inconvenience, reported Nov 2026).
